report.summary: Reviewed publish.py chunk 3 of 4, enumerating all claims and observations.
risks: screen_egress | medium | secret_floor_rule called with empty text for paths; if floor treats empty as no-match, empty paths silently pass; if it matches empty, every call refuses. | Inspect secret_floor_rule to see how it handles empty input.

_classify_failure | medium | Substring matching on lowercased stderr/stdout may match 'not found' in unrelated context (e.g., 'file not found' from a different tool), misclassifying as PR not found. | Add a test with a stderr containing 'not found' but not related to PR.

load_for_publish verdict vendors_answered | medium | When answered is empty, vendors_answered becomes requested, implying all requested answered when none did. | Confirm whether empty answered should yield empty list instead of fallback to requested.

_parse_comment | low | Tolerant parsing may silently drop fields if gh changes shape; author fallback to 'user' may mask missing author. | Add a test with a comment lacking both author and user fields.

handoff.purpose: Egress gate, failure classification, load_for_publish, publish_to_pr, read_pr_thread.

symbols.name: screen_egress
symbols.note: Runs secret_floor_rule on evidence paths and channel texts; returns (channel, rule) for first hit or None.

symbols.name: _gh_argv
symbols.note: Appends --repo flag to base argv if repo is provided.

symbols.name: _classify_failure
symbols.note: Maps a failed RunResult to (status, detail) using substring matching on stderr/stdout.

symbols.name: _first_url
symbols.note: Extracts first http(s) URL token from text.

symbols.name: load_for_publish
symbols.note: Reconstructs (verdict, turns) from a stored bus transcript via bus.load_transcript.

symbols.name: publish_to_pr
symbols.note: Renders markdown, runs egress gate, and posts comment via gh subprocess unless dry_run.

symbols.note: Parses one gh comment object into a PRTurn; tolerant of author shapes.

claims.text: Returns ``(channel, rule)`` for the FIRST hit, or None if clean.
claims.why: Code iterates paths then channels, returning on first hit; returns None at end.

claims.text: The returned rule is a fixed label / path fragment from ``sensitivity`` -- never matched text, so a refusal can be logged and reported without re-leaking the secret it refused (memstore's ``_scan_secret`` posture, same floor, same reason).
claims.why: The nature of secret_floor_rule's return value is not visible in this chunk; it is defined in another module.

claims.text: Auth is tested before not-found because GitHub answers 404 -- not 403 -- for a private repo you are not authenticated to see; classifying that as ``pr_not_found`` would send an operator hunting for a PR that exists and is merely invisible to a logged-out CLI.
claims.why: The auth checks appear before the not-found checks in the if/elif chain.

claims.text: ``(verdict, turns)`` reconstructed from a stored bus transcript.
claims.why: load_for_publish calls bus.load_transcript and builds a verdict dict from the records.

claims.text: Only what the bus actually recorded. The council package stores no ``outcome`` and no ``convergence`` field -- by construction, because it promotes nothing -- so none is invented here, and :func:`render_markdown` prints "(not recorded)" for them.
claims.why: The absence of outcome/convergence fields in the bus and render_markdown's behavior are not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Quorum comes from the roster records' ``participants``: a vendor is ANSWERED only if it actually produced a turn, not if it was merely seated.
claims.why: Code only adds to answered when a turn's status is 'spoke' and the vendor is present; roster participants are added to requested only.

claims.text: That is the distinction the degraded-quorum banner is built on, so deriving it from the seat list would silently upgrade every short council to a full one.
claims.why: The degraded-quorum banner logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Render the deliberation and post it as a PR comment. Never raises for an operational failure -- every outcome is a status in ``PUBLISH_STATUSES``.
claims.why: The claim about never raising depends on render_markdown and other functions not shown; the function itself only returns PublishResult, but exceptions could propagate from render_markdown or screen_egress.

claims.text: ``dry_run=True`` renders and gates but does NOT invoke the runner at all; the markdown comes back on the result.
claims.why: When dry_run is True, the function returns PublishResult(status=STATUS_DRY_RUN, markdown=body) before calling the runner.

claims.text: The gate still runs, so a dry run is an honest rehearsal rather than a way around the floor.
claims.why: screen_egress is invoked before the dry_run check.

claims.text: The body goes to gh on STDIN via ``--body-file -``: a deliberation exceeds the Windows argv limit, and stdin keeps the payload inspectable by a fake runner in tests exactly as argv would be.
claims.why: argv is ['gh', 'pr', 'comment', pr, '--body-file', '-'] and run(argv, body) passes body as stdin.

claims.text: Read the PR's comments back as structured turns, so a later council round can consume what a human or another agent replied.
claims.why: read_pr_thread parses comments into PRTurn objects and returns them in ThreadResult.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure; every outcome is a status in ``READ_STATUSES``.
claims.why: All paths return ThreadResult; no exceptions are raised in the visible code (json.loads is caught).

claims.text: Nothing read here is authoritative: a reply is INPUT to a later round, not a verdict, and it is not on the hash-chained bus until the council appends it there.
claims.why: The bus appending behavior is not in this chunk.

claims.text: One gh comment object -> one PRTurn. Tolerant of the two author shapes gh uses (``author.login`` from the GraphQL-backed ``pr view --json``, ``user.login`` from the REST-backed ``gh api``).
claims.why: The implementation is cut off at the end of the chunk; the author-shape handling is not fully visible.

claims.text: A check that CANNOT FAIL: an assertion comparing something with itself, a test whose fixture is derived from the thing under test, a branch no input reaches.
claims.why: No such check is present in this chunk.

claims.text: A refusal with NO REACHABLE REPAIR: code that reports an error and names a fix another rule in this same file forbids.
claims.why: No such refusal is present in this chunk.

claims.text: A rule INVERTED with respect to its own stated goal: it blocks the narrow precise action and permits the broad one.
claims.why: No such rule is present in this chunk.

claims.text: A value parsed from output whose FORMAT IS NOT PINNED: a parser that will silently report 'absent' rather than 'unreadable' when its input changes shape.
claims.why: The parsing code is incomplete in this chunk; cannot determine if it silently defaults on shape changes.

observations.what: In screen_egress, paths are passed to secret_floor_rule with empty string as the second argument. If secret_floor_rule expects a text to scan, an empty text may always match or never match depending on implementation.
In _classify_failure, the substring 'not found' is used to classify PR not found. This could match unrelated errors like 'file not found' from a different tool, causing misclassification.
In load_for_publish, when answered is empty, vendors_answered is set to requested, which would report all requested vendors as answered. This could be misleading if no vendor actually spoke.

In publish_to_pr, the egress gate runs before checking for a PR reference. This means a dry_run with no PR will still run the gate, which is fine, but the detail message for dry run does not mention the missing PR.

In read_pr_thread, the egress gate runs before checking for a PR reference. This means a read with no PR will still run the gate, which is fine, but the detail message for missing PR does not mention the gate.
